learningObjective: Distinguish post-training quantization (PTQ) from quantization-aware training (QAT).

canonicalClaims.claim: PTQ quantizes a pre-trained FP model without further training, using a calibration set to determine scales; QAT inserts fake-quantization ops during training so weights become robust to quantization noise, typically at higher cost but higher low-bit-width accuracy.
conditions: PTQ requires a representative calibration set for activation scales.
QAT requires a full training loop with quantization-aware ops.
nonImplications: Does not imply QAT is always better; INT8 PTQ often matches QAT.
Does not imply PTQ is entirely training-free; per-layer weight optimization (GPTQ) does update weights, just not via full backprop.

misconceptions.claim: PTQ and QAT differ only in the target bit width (INT8 vs INT4).
misconceptions.whyWrong: Both can target any bit width; the distinction is training-time involvement.

misconceptions.claim: PTQ is applied at runtime during serving; QAT is applied offline.
misconceptions.whyWrong: PTQ is an offline process (calibrate, freeze, deploy); the 'post-training' refers to timing relative to model training, not inference.

misconceptions.claim: QAT always yields a bit-exact quantized model with no accuracy loss.
misconceptions.whyWrong: QAT reduces accuracy loss but does not eliminate it; residual gap depends on bit width and workload.

misconceptions.claim: PTQ is universally applicable to all models; QAT is only needed for CNNs.
misconceptions.whyWrong: QAT applies to any architecture; the choice between PTQ and QAT depends on target accuracy and bit width.

implementationFacts: PyTorch supports both PTQ (`torch.ao.quantization.prepare` + calibration) and QAT (`torch.ao.quantization.prepare_qat`).
TensorRT supports PTQ via calibration; QAT integration via ONNX Q/DQ nodes.
performanceScenarios: INT8 ImageNet ResNet-50: PTQ typically loses <0.5% top-1 vs FP32.
INT4 LLM: QAT-based approaches reach lower perplexity than pure PTQ round-to-nearest.
